transforms.name: lexer
transforms.sanitization: Identifies token boundaries; no regex escaping

transforms.name: parse
transforms.description: Converts lex tokens to semantic tokens; generates default patterns for :name parameters
transforms.sanitization: safePattern() generates default regex patterns for parameters; restricts nested groups to non-capturing

transforms.name: safePattern
transforms.input: prevText (from preceding path literal or prefix)
transforms.description: Generates default capture pattern for unnamed parameters. When prevText is a non-delimiter, generates negative lookahead pattern.
transforms.sanitization: Escapes delimiter and prevText in regex via escapeString()

transforms.name: tokensToRegexp
transforms.description: Compiles semantic tokens into a complete regex string with anchors, delimiters, and capture groups
transforms.sanitization: escapeString() applied to string tokens, prefixes, suffixes, delimiter, endsWith

transforms.name: regex_compilation
transforms.description: Compiles the generated regex string into a executable RegExp
transforms.sanitization: None — regex string is used as-is

transforms.name: encode_transform
transforms.description: User-provided encode function transforms values before regex embedding or path construction
transforms.sanitization: escapeString() applied after encoding in tokensToRegexp

trust_boundaries.name: path_to_regex
trust_boundaries.description: User path string content is transformed into regex pattern via safePattern(). User-controlled path structure (adjacent parameters with non-delimiter separators) influences the complexity of the generated regex.
trust_boundaries.guard: escapeString() for literal tokens; safePattern() generates patterns for parameters; no complexity analysis of generated regex

trust_boundaries.name: regex_match
trust_boundaries.description: User pathname is matched against generated regex. Input length and content interact with regex structure to determine execution time.
trust_boundaries.guard: None — regex.exec() with no timeout or complexity bounds

trust_boundaries.name: options_to_charclass
trust_boundaries.description: Delimiter and endsWith options are embedded in regex character classes [...]. Unescaped metacharacters (especially -) corrupt the character class semantics.
trust_boundaries.guard: escapeString() — but does not escape the - character

flows.name: path_to_executable_regex
flows.description: Path string → lexer → parse → safePattern → tokensToRegexp → new RegExp → re.exec

flows.name: data_to_path_template
flows.description: Data values → encode → validate against regex → path string concatenation

flows.name: options_to_regex_charclass
flows.description: delimiter/endsWith options → escapeString → regex character class in route

findings.path: SRC-1(path_string) → TF-1(lexer) → TF-2(parse) → TF-3(safePattern) → TF-4(tokensToRegexp) → TF-5(new RegExp) → SNK-2(re.exec)
findings.evidence: When a path string contains two adjacent parameters separated by a non-delimiter character (e.g. '/:a-:b'), the safePattern() function at line 184 generates a negative lookahead pattern: (?:(?!${escapeString(prevText)})[^${escapeString(delimiter)}])+?. This pattern has a structural property where: (1) the negative lookahead (?!X) is zero-width and re-evaluates at every position, (2) the character class [^delimiter]+? is a lazy quantifier that backtracks, (3) the combination creates multiplicative complexity — for input length n with repeated separator characters, the regex engine explores O(2^n) match states. The input '/a-aaaa...-a' (n repetitions of 'a-' followed by 'a') causes the regex engine to spend exponential time exploring match positions for the (?:(?!-)[^/])+? pattern before concluding no match exists. The transform from path tokens (TF-3 safePattern) does not analyze or bound the computational complexity of the generated regex. The trust boundary between library pattern generation and regex engine execution has no guard for execution time.
findings.missing_guard: The safePattern() function must either: (1) avoid generating patterns with nested quantifiers and zero-width assertions, (2) analyze the generated regex for worst-case complexity before compilation, or (3) use atomic groups/possessive quantifiers to prevent backtracking. The current pattern (?:(?!X)[^Y])+? should be replaced with a possessive or atomic equivalent such as [^Y]*(?:(?!X)[^Y]+)* or a single-pass [^XY]+ pattern.

findings.path: SRC-4(options.delimiter) → TF-4(tokensToRegexp escapeString) → SNK-1(regex character class [...])
findings.evidence: The escapeString() function (line 439) does not escape the '-' character, which is a range operator inside regex character classes [...]. If delimiter contains '-' (e.g. 'a-z'), the character class [^a-z] is interpreted as 'not lowercase letters' instead of 'not a, not -, not z'. However, delimiter and endsWith are typically set by the application developer in code, not derived from user input at runtime. The trust level of these options is SEMI_TRUSTED — they come from configuration, not direct user input. While the missing escape is technically a bug in escapeString(), the practical attack surface is minimal because: (1) delimiters are typically single characters like '/', (2) application developers control these options, (3) an attacker would need to influence the application's configuration to exploit this. Classified as FALSE_POSITIVE because the trust boundary analysis shows the options do not typically cross from UNTRUSTED to TRUSTED.
findings.missing_guard: escapeString() should include '-' in its escape list for completeness, but this is a defense-in-depth improvement rather than a security-critical fix given the trust model of the options.
